text: ∫_(A > 0) det(A)^(a−(p+1)/2) e^(−tr A) dA = Γ_p(a) over the positive-definite p × p matrices for a > (p−1)/2, announced two days ago in dimension 0 only and now in every dimension: [Lebesgue measure on the cone is the pushforward under L ↦ LLᵀ](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/SymmetricMatrix/Cholesky.html#TauCeti.map_cholesky_symmetricLebesgue) of Lebesgue measure on positive-diagonal lower-triangular L weighted by 2^p ∏ L_ii^(p−i); the Wishart normalising constant (Muirhead, Thms 2.1.9, 2.1.14).

name: Burnside's basis theorem for pro-p groups
text: a subset of a pro-p group G topologically generates G exactly when its image topologically generates G/Φ_p(G), since a proper closed subgroup lies in an open normal subgroup of index p; the theorem the Frattini subgroup Φ_p(G) of TauCeti#6649 exists for (Ribes–Zalesskii, §2.8).

name: Topologically finitely generated profinite groups are Hopfian
text: a continuous surjective endomorphism of such a group has trivial kernel and is a topological automorphism, by counting the open subgroups of each index; the shift on ∏_ℕ F shows finite generation cannot be dropped (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, Prop. 2.5.2).

name: A number field is discrete in its adele ring
text: the diagonal copy of K in 𝔸_K is a discrete closed subgroup and 𝔸_K/K is Hausdorff, the neighbourhood of 0 meeting K only in 0 being the adeles of norm < 1 at every infinite place and integral at every finite place; compactness of 𝔸_K/K is the next step (Cassels–Fröhlich, II §14).

name: Frobenius functionals and the Nakayama automorphism
text: a functional φ on a finite-dimensional algebra A with (a, b) ↦ φ(ab) nondegenerate, making A a Frobenius algebra: one exists exactly when A ≅ Hom_k(A, k) as right A-modules, the [Nakayama automorphism](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Algebra/Frobenius/Basic.html#LinearMap.IsFrobeniusFunctional.nakayamaAut) ν with φ(ab) = φ(b ν(a)) is a unique algebra automorphism, trivial exactly when φ is symmetric, and A is injective as a left and as a right module over itself (Lam, *Lectures on Modules and Rings*, §16).

name: The quantile function and inverse transform sampling
text: F_μ⁻¹(t) = inf{x | t ≤ F_μ(x)} for a law μ on ℝ, and F_μ⁻¹ pushes the uniform law on (0, 1) forward to μ; reading two quantile functions off one uniform variable gives the [monotone coupling](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Quantile.html#MeasureTheory.Measure.quantileCoupling) of two real laws, whence W_p(μ, ν) ≤ ‖F_μ⁻¹ − F_ν⁻¹‖_(L^p(0,1)) for every p ∈ [1, ∞]; equality is still to come (Villani, §2.2).

name: Linear codes
text: a linear code as a subspace of Fⁿ presented by a generator matrix (row space) or a parity-check matrix (kernel), compatible exactly when HGᵀ = 0; monomial and permutation equivalence of codes, preserving Hamming weight, distance, dimension and weight distribution; and the [Euclidean dual C^⊥](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/InformationTheory/Coding/EuclideanDual.html#Submodule.euclideanDual) with (C^⊥)^⊥ = C, dim C + dim C^⊥ = n and #C · #C^⊥ = qⁿ (Huffman–Pless, §§1.2–1.6).

name: The Teichmüller lift of a local field
text: for a nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝓀 of order q, the unique multiplicative section 𝓀ˣ → 𝒪ˣ of reduction with values in the (q−1)-torsion, whose image is exactly μ_(q−1), so reduction identifies μ_(q−1)(K) with 𝓀ˣ; built from Hensel's lemma via μₙ(R) ≅ μₙ(R/𝔪) for a Henselian local domain R with n invertible, unlike Mathlib's `Perfection.teichmuller` (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, II §4).

name: Hilbert 90 for infinite Galois extensions, and the Kummer isomorphism
text: for every Galois extension L/K, finite or infinite, the continuous cohomology H¹(Gal(L/K), Lˣ) vanishes, so H¹(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ) = 0 and, for n invertible in K, a ↦ [g ↦ g(α)/α] with αⁿ = a is an isomorphism [Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ ≅ H¹(G_K, μₙ)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.html#TauCeti.kummerIso); Mathlib's finite-layer Hilbert 90 is the input at each finite level (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, 6.2.1).

name: The splitting criterion for quaternion algebras
text: over a field K with 2 invertible and a, b ∈ Kˣ, the following are equivalent: ℍ[K,a,b] ≅ M₂(K); b is a norm from K[T]/(T² − a); b = x² − ay² is solvable; ⟨1, −a, −b⟩ is isotropic; the norm form ⟨1, −a, −b, ab⟩ is isotropic; and every such algebra is either split or a division algebra (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, III.2.7, III.4.2; Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, III.1).

name: The Cartan matrix of an Artinian ring
text: over an Artinian ring R the indecomposable projective classes form a ℤ-basis of K₀(proj R) with Krull–Schmidt multiplicities as coordinates, the pairing ⟨[P_i], [M]⟩ = [M : S_i] against the simple-class basis of G₀(mod R) is perfect, the Cartan map has matrix C_ij = [P_j : S_i], and [det C = ±1](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GrothendieckGroup/UnimodularCartanMatrix.html#TauCeti.cartanMatrix_det_eq_one_or_neg_one) whenever every finitely generated module has a finite projective resolution, Eilenberg's theorem, with the sign left open (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, III.3).

name: Corestriction in group cohomology
text: for a subgroup S ≤ G of finite index, the transfer Hⁿ(S, Res A) → Hⁿ(G, A) in every degree, built through Shapiro's lemma and the trace Coind Res A → A, natural in A and with cor ∘ res = [G : S]; on the way Mathlib's Shapiro isomorphism is identified as restriction followed by evaluation at 1 (Brown, *Cohomology of Groups*, III §9).

name: The center of a semisimple group is finite
text: the scheme-theoretic center of a semisimple affine group scheme over a field is finite over that field, in every characteristic and with no reducedness assumption on the center, the finiteness input for the central isogeny onto the adjoint group (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*; Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §8.1).

name: The structure of the multiplicative group of a local field
text: for a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of order q, a uniformizer ϖ gives a topological isomorphism Kˣ ≅ ℤ × 𝒪ˣ, x ↦ (v(x), xϖ^(−v(x))), and the Teichmüller lift gives the canonical 𝒪ˣ ≅ μ_(q−1) × U⁽¹⁾, so Kˣ ≅ ℤ × μ_(q−1) × U⁽¹⁾ (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, II §§4–5; Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II.5.3). Beside it, [a finite extension of a nonarchimedean local field is again one](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/FiniteExtension.html#TauCeti.finiteExtension_isNonarchimedeanLocalField), the spectral norm being its unique extended absolute value, and the containment half of the local square theorem: [every unit of depth 2v(2) + 1 is a square](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Squares.html#TauCeti.unitFiltration_le_range_powMonoidHom_two), so (Kˣ)² is open, dyadic fields included (O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, 63:1).

name: The smooth local geodesic flow
text: on a finite-dimensional boundaryless manifold, [the maximal flow of a C^(n+1) vector field is jointly C^(n+1) in initial point and time near (x₀, 0)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/IntegralCurve/SmoothDependence.html#TauCeti.contMDiffAt_maximalIntegralCurve), the local half of the fundamental theorem on flows, and the geodesic spray of a Riemannian manifold has a jointly smooth local flow on TM whose projections are the geodesics with prescribed initial data; the interface follows the open mathlib4#26394, and the global flow and exponential map come next (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 9.12; do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3 §2).

name: The function field of an elliptic curve has genus one
text: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over any field F, F(W) has genus one with exact constant field F, read off from L(n·O) = {p + qy : 2 deg p ≤ n, 2 deg q + 3 ≤ n} and Riemann's theorem; so Mathlib's elliptic curves are elliptic function fields in the sense of yesterday's TauCeti#6812 (Stichtenoth, Prop 6.1.3; Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3).

name: The Kauffman bracket
text: the state sum ⟨D⟩ = Σ_s a^(A(s)−B(s)) δ^(loops(s)−1), δ = −(a² + a⁻²), of a planar-diagram code, invariant under relabelling, the mirror image inverting a, ⟨c circles⟩ = δ^(c−1) and ⟨kink⟩ = −a³; invariance under the Reidemeister moves, and with it the Jones polynomial, is not yet there (Kauffman, *State models and the Jones polynomial*, Topology 26 (1987)).

name: Dedekind's theorem
text: for an algebraic integer θ whose minimal polynomial f over ℤ is squarefree mod p, an arithmetic Frobenius at a prime above p in a Galois number field splitting f permutes the roots of f with cycle type the degrees of the irreducible factors of f mod p, fixed roots counted as 1-cycles; in polynomial form, [for monic f ∈ ℤ[X] with p ∤ disc f, Gal(f) contains an element of exactly that cycle type](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Frobenius/CycleType.html#TauCeti.NumberField.exists_gal_fullCycleType_eq_factorizationType). On the way, a Frobenius and inertia generate the decomposition group at ramified primes too, extending TauCeti#5602 (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §8 Ex. 4–5).

name: Strong approximation for the finite adele ring
text: for any Dedekind domain R with fraction field K, K is dense in the finite adele ring 𝔸_K^f: an element of K approximates a given finite adele at finitely many places while staying integral elsewhere, so 𝔸_K^f = K + ∏ 𝒪_v; Mathlib has the matching density at the infinite places of a number field (Cassels–Fröhlich, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II §15).

name: Dedekind's different theorem, both halves
text: for a finite separable extension of algebraic function fields and a place P′ over P, d(P′|P) = e(P′|P) − 1 exactly when P′ is tame (separable residue extension, e prime to the residue characteristic) and d ≥ e exactly when it is wild, without assuming a perfect constant field; the tame direction was TauCeti#5807, and underneath is [P^e ∣ 𝔡(B/A) iff the residue extension at P is inseparable or e vanishes in A/p](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Different.html#TauCeti.pow_ramificationIdx_dvd_differentIdeal_iff), where Mathlib has P ∣ 𝔡 iff ramified and P^(e−1) ∣ 𝔡 (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.5.1, Cor 3.5.5).

name: The Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality for C¹ functions on a convex domain
text: for Ω bounded convex open in an n-dimensional real normed space with Haar measure, S ⊆ Ω of positive measure, u ∈ C¹(Ω) and 1 ≤ p < ∞, ‖u − ⨍_S u‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)} ≤ |B(0,1)| (diam Ω)^(n+1) / |S| · ‖Du‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)}, via [Schur's test for integral operators](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Integral/SchurTest.html#TauCeti.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_mul_le), also new; the constant is not sharp, and the W^{1,p} version waits on Meyers–Serrin (Gilbarg–Trudinger, (7.45)).

name: The Weyl module 𝕊^μ(kⁿ) is an irreducible representation of GLₙ(k)
text: in characteristic zero, the image of a Young symmetrizer of shape μ on (kⁿ)^{⊗|μ|} is irreducible under GLₙ(k) exactly when μ has at most n rows, so the [Schur functor](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups/WeylModule/Irreducible.html#TauCeti.simple_schurFunctor_iff) of TauCeti#1751 takes simple values there, by an annihilator comparison in k[S_d] and Schur–Weyl duality (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Thm 6.3).

name: Atkin–Lehner operators commute with the good Hecke operators
text: for Q ∥ N the normalized involution 𝒲_Q on M_k(Γ₀(N)) and on S_k(Γ₀(N)) commutes with the Hecke operator of every Γ₀(N) double coset whose determinant is coprime to Q, since the Atkin–Lehner matrix normalizes Γ₀(N) and fixes each such double coset; the identification with the classical Tₙ is next (Atkin–Lehner, Math. Ann. 185 (1970); Shimura, §3.4).

name: The Frobenius trace at bad reduction is 1, −1 or 0
text: over the fraction field of a DVR with residue field of size q, the trace a = q + 1 − #W̃(𝔽_q) of the reduction of a minimal Weierstrass equation, singular point included, is 1, −1, 0 at split multiplicative, nonsplit multiplicative and additive reduction in every characteristic, so Mathlib's case-defined [local polynomial is 1 − aT + qT² at good and 1 − aT at bad reduction](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/LocalPolynomial.html#WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial_eq_of_not_hasGoodReduction) (Silverman, *AEC*, VII.5, App. C.16).

name: Dedekind's criterion
text: for an integral primitive element θ with f = minpoly ℤ θ and f ≡ ∏ φᵢ^{eᵢ} mod p, write f − ∏ Φᵢ^{eᵢ} = pH for lifts Φᵢ; then p ∤ [𝓞_K : ℤ[θ]] exactly when for every i either eᵢ = 1 or φᵢ ∤ H mod p, independently of the lifts. Beside it, [p stays prime in the Dedekind–Kummer setting exactly when the minimal polynomial is irreducible mod p](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/KummerDedekind.html#TauCeti.KummerDedekind.Ideal.irreducible_map_iff_irreducible_minpoly), closing a TODO in Mathlib (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, Thm 6.1.4).

name: The Hilbert symbol
text: (a, b) = +1 or −1 according as b = x² − a y² is solvable, over any field; with 2 invertible it is +1 exactly when [the quaternion algebra (a, b) splits](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/HilbertSymbol/Basic.html#TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_eq_one_iff_nonempty_algEquiv_matrix), equivalently when ⟨1, −a, −b⟩ is isotropic; it is symmetric and depends only on square classes (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, III §1; Lam, III.2.7).

name: Eisenstein series with character
text: for Dirichlet characters ψ mod u and φ mod v, weight k ≥ 3 and uv ∣ N, G_k^{ψ,φ}(z) = Σ_{(c,d)} ψ(c) φ⁻¹(d) (cvz + d)^(−k) is a modular form for Γ₁(N) lying in the nebentypus space M_k(N, ψφ), zero unless ψ(−1)φ(−1) = (−1)^k; the normalization E_k^{ψ,φ} and its q-expansion come next (Diamond–Shurman, *A First Course in Modular Forms*, §4.5).

name: Linear codes: generator and parity-check matrices, minimum distance, weight enumerators

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#6778, TauCeti#6869, TauCeti#7337, TauCeti#6873, TauCeti#7160, TauCeti#7195

text: codes generated and checked by matrices, with rank formulas and [I | A] against [−Aᵀ | I]; the [minimum Hamming distance](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/InformationTheory/Coding/MinimumDistance.html#Set.hammingMinDist) as the least nonzero weight of an additive code; the weight enumerator W_C(X, Y) = Σ_w A_w X^(n−w) Y^w, multiplicative on direct sums; duals of punctured and shortened codes, Hermitian duality and information sets, with the MacWilliams identity next; minimum distance is also being formalised in mathlib4#38014 (Huffman–Pless, *Fundamentals of Error-Correcting Codes*, Ch. 1, §7.2).

name: Riemann–Roch for a proper curve
text: χ(𝒪_X(D)) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ = deg D + 1 − g for a Weil divisor on a proper integral curve with a rational point and discrete valuation rings in codimension one, with deg D = Σ_y D(y)·[κ(y):k] and g = dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X); finite-dimensionality of H¹ is still a hypothesis, and Serre duality is not there yet (Hartshorne IV.1.3).

name: The Weyl character formula
text: ch(M)·∏_{α>0}(1 − e^(−α)) = Σ_{w∈W} sgn(w)·e^(w·λ) for a finite-dimensional module generated by a highest-weight vector of weight λ over a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, proved with no order on the scalars, chamber arguments replaced by inversion sets (Humphreys §24).

name: The Wiener–Ikehara theorem
text: for nonnegative coefficients whose Dirichlet series converges on Re s > 1 and differs from κ/(s − 1) by a function continuous on Re s ≥ 1, x⁻¹·Σ_{n ≤ x} a(n) → κ, with the natural-cutoff and shifted-abscissa variants (Korevaar, *Tauberian Theory*, Ch. III).

name: The Hurwitz genus formula
text: [k′:k]·(2g′ − 2) = [F′:F]·(2g − 2) + [k′:k]·deg Diff(F′/F) for a finite separable extension of function fields, from the cotrace identity (Cotr ω) = Con(ω) + Diff, with the tame bound and its equality criterion, g ≤ g′, and ramification of every extension of k(x) of degree above one when k is the full constant field (Stichtenoth 3.4.13).

name: The binary Golay codes
text: the extended [24, 12, 8] code of the generator [I₁₂ | B], self-dual and doubly even, enumerator X²⁴ + 759X¹⁶Y⁸ + 2576X¹²Y¹² + 759X⁸Y¹⁶ + Y²⁴, and its [23, 12, 7] puncture at every coordinate, recovered by the parity extension; every finite check is a kernel computation (Conway–Sloane, Ch. 3).

name: The MacWilliams identity
text: #C·W_{C⊥}(X, Y) = W_C(X + (q − 1)Y, X − Y) in ℤ[X, Y] for a linear code over a field of q elements, with the Krawtchouk form #C·A_w(C⊥) = Σ_j A_j(C)·K_w(j) (MacWilliams–Sloane, Ch. 5).

name: Morrey's inequality and the Morrey embedding
text: for p > n a C¹ function with Lᵖ derivative is Hölder of exponent 1 − n/p with an explicit constant, every u ∈ W^(1,p)(ℝⁿ) agrees a.e. with such a function, and the induced map into C^(0,1−n/p)(ℝⁿ) is bounded and injective; the borderline p = n is open (Evans §5.6).

name: Marcinkiewicz interpolation
text: between two finite endpoints: a subadditive operator of weak type (p₀, p₀) and (p₁, p₁) is of strong type (p, p) for p₀ < p < p₁, with explicit constants degenerating at each end (Stein–Weiss, Ch. V).

name: The Herglotz representation theorem
text: a function holomorphic on the unit disc has nonnegative real part exactly when it is w ↦ ∫ (z + w)/(z − w) dμ(z) + i·Im F(0) for a finite measure on the circle, built on Mathlib's Poisson and Herglotz–Riesz kernels (Duren, Ch. 1).

name: The Schwarz–Christoffel mapping theorem, convex case
text: for ordered prevertices with exponents in (−1, 0) summing to −2 the primitive maps the upper half-plane bijectively onto the polygon's interior, by showing it is a covering map off the boundary path; the non-convex case and the parameter problem remain (Driscoll–Trefethen, Ch. 2).

name: Metric completeness gives geodesic completeness
text: in a Riemannian manifold complete for its Riemannian distance every maximal geodesic is defined for all time, so the exponential map is defined on the whole tangent space; this is one arrow of Hopf–Rinow, not the equivalence (do Carmo 7.2.8).

name: The Grothendieck–Witt and Witt rings of a field
text: GW(K) as the Grothendieck ring of regular quadratic forms and W(K) as its quotient by the hyperbolic ideal, two forms having the same Witt class exactly when their anisotropic parts are isometric (Lam II §1).

name: Dedekind's theorem on factorization modulo primes
text: at a prime not dividing the discriminant the Galois image contains an element whose cycle type is the factorization type of f mod p, with the criteria that then give Aₙ and Sₙ, worked on x⁵ − x − 1; the transitive subgroups of Sₙ are classified for n ≤ 5 too, and an irreducible cubic has group A₃ or S₃ by its discriminant (van der Waerden §61).

name: The Fricke functional equation and the Atkin–Lehner sign
text: Λ_N(k − s, f) = i^k·Λ_N(s, g) for the completed L-function; a newform of trivial nebentypus has Fricke eigenvalue ±1; and Tₙ* = χ(n)⁻¹Tₙ on S_k(N, χ) for (n, N) = 1 (Diamond–Shurman §5.10).

name: The class group of a curve is its Picard group
text: every line bundle on a Noetherian integral scheme of dimension at most one with discrete valuation rings in codimension one is the sheaf 𝒪_X(D) of a Weil divisor, so Cl(X) → Pic(X) is an isomorphism (Hartshorne II.6.16).

name: The Caccioppoli inequality
text: ∫ψ²‖∇u‖² ≤ (2Λ/λ)²∫‖∇ψ‖²u² + (2/λ)∫ψ²fu for a weak solution of a divergence-form uniformly elliptic equation, with constants depending only on the ellipticity bounds (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Ch. 8).

name: The Clifford correspondence, irreducibility half
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, inducing to G an irreducible representation of the inertia group of an irreducible representation of a normal subgroup gives an irreducible one; the bijection is still to come (Isaacs 6.11).

name: Multiplicativity of the Herbrand quotient
text: the quotient announced with TauCeti#5764 is multiplicative in a short exact sequence of representations of a finite cyclic group, by the exact hexagon of Tate cohomology, and unchanged by a map with finite kernel and cokernel (Neukirch IV §7).

name: Class formations and their fundamental classes
text: the Artin–Tate axioms in finite-layer form, with H²(K/F) cyclic of order [K:F] generated by the class of invariant 1/[K:F], and the hypotheses of Tate's theorem available for every subgroup; reciprocity is not claimed (Artin–Tate XIV).

name: Dummit's solvability criterion for quintics
text: a monic irreducible separable quintic over any field has solvable Galois group if and only if its F₂₀ resolvent sextic has a root in the base field, provided that sextic is separable (Dummit, *Solving solvable quintics*, Math. Comp. 57 (1991), Thm 1); it rests on the general [resolvent root criterion](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/Resolvent/Root.html#TauCeti.ResolventSpec.exists_isRoot_specialize_iff_exists_le_map_conj), that the resolvent for H ≤ Sₙ has a root in F exactly when the Galois image is conjugate into H (Cohen §6.3), and on a transitive subgroup of S₅ being solvable iff it lies in a conjugate of F₂₀.

name: Kostant's multiplicity formula
text: dim M_μ = Σ_{w∈W} sgn(w)·P(w(λ+ρ) − (μ+ρ)) for a finite-dimensional module generated by a highest-weight vector of weight λ over a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, P the Kostant partition function, read off from the Weyl character formula of TauCeti#7644 by dividing by the Weyl denominator coefficient by coefficient (Humphreys §24.2, Kostant 1959); the statement for the irreducible L(λ) itself waits on the injectivity half of PBW.

name: Mixed Hodge structures form an abelian category
text: with rational Hodge morphisms, assembled from binary products with componentwise weight and Hodge filtrations (new here) and the kernels, cokernels and coimage–image comparison that strictness provided (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 2.3.5).

name: Weierstrass division for restricted power series
text: over a complete nonarchimedean field, if f is restricted and distinguished of degree s at a radius c (its Gauss norm at c is attained in degree s and every later coefficient is strictly smaller), every restricted series g is uniquely g = q·f + r with q restricted and r a polynomial of degree below s; existence lands here and, with the norm identity and uniqueness of TauCeti#7664, completes Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert §5.2.1 Thm 2. Mathlib's `PowerSeries.IsWeierstrassDivisionAt` is the adic-order variant, and neither statement implies the other.

name: Lattice-point counting with a boundary-order error
text: for a ℤ-lattice L in an n-dimensional real normed space, a Haar measure μ and a bounded set D whose frontier is Lipschitz parametrizable in dimension n − 1, #(c·D ∩ L) = μ(D)/covol(L) · cⁿ + O(c^(n−1)) as c → ∞, from a cell decomposition and the count #((c·S + B) ∩ L) ≤ A·c^d for S Lipschitz parametrizable in dimension d (Lang, *Algebraic Number Theory* VI §2); Mathlib's `ZLattice.covolume.tendsto_card_div_pow'` gives the leading term with no error.

name: Every graphon is representable on the unit interval
text: a graphon on an arbitrary probability space is at cut distance zero from a graphon on ([0, 1], Lebesgue): joint measurability lets it factor as W(x, y) = V(q(x), q(y)) through a measurable map q to the Cantor space, so it is a pullback from a standard Borel carrier (Janson, *Graphons, cut norm and distance*, Thm 7.1 and Lemma 7.3).

name: The Nevanlinna representation of Pick functions
text: a function holomorphic on the upper half-plane with nonnegative imaginary part is F(z) = b·z + ∫_ℝ (1 + xz)/(x − z) dρ(x) + Re F(i) with b ≥ 0 and ρ a finite positive measure on ℝ, obtained from the Herglotz representation of TauCeti#7513 by the Cayley map z ↦ (z − i)/(z + i) and the boundary Cayley homeomorphism ℝ ≃ S¹ ∖ {1}, splitting off the atom at 1 (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Ch. 6).

name: The semi-local decomposition at a finite place
text: for an extension L/K of number fields and a finite place v of K, K_v ⊗_K L ≅ ∏_{w ∣ v} L_w as K_v-algebras with a ⊗ x ↦ (a·x)_w, hence [Σ_{w ∣ v} [L_w : K_v] = [L : K]](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/LocalGlobal/Semilocal/Basic.html#TauCeti.sum_finrank_adicCompletion_eq_finrank), the finite-place counterpart of Mathlib's `NumberField.InfinitePlace.sum_inertiaDeg_eq_finrank` (Neukirch II (8.3)).

name: Shimizu's lemma
text: if a discrete subgroup Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ) contains the translation z ↦ z + w, every element of Γ with lower-left entry c ≠ 0 has |c| ≥ |w|⁻¹, equivalently (g·z).im · z.im ≤ w² whenever g ∈ Γ does not fix ∞ (Jørgensen's proof, Beardon §5.4); hence horodiscs of height at least the cusp width are [precisely invariant](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Fuchsian/Cusp/Horodisc.html#TauCeti.Subgroup.CuspDatum.mem_stabilizer_of_mem_horodisc_of_smul_mem_horodisc) under the cusp stabilizer.

name: A separable isogeny is unramified
text: for a separable isogeny φ of elliptic curves, every place of the source function field is unramified over the target, since both have genus one and the Hurwitz formula forces the different to vanish; hence Σ_{P′ ∣ P} f(P′ ∣ P) = deg φ, and over a separably closed constant field every place has exactly deg φ places above it (Silverman II.5.9, III.4.10).

name: Construction A and the Golay lattice
text: the Construction A lattice of a code C ≤ (ℤ/m)ⁿ is even exactly when 2m ∣ Σ zᵢ² for every integer lift of a codeword (for m = 2: C doubly even), its discriminant is mⁿ/#C² for self-orthogonal C, and for the extended binary Golay code of TauCeti#7570 it is a positive-definite even unimodular lattice of rank 24 (Ebeling §1.3, Conway–Sloane Ch. 7).

name: The fundamental ideal of the Witt ring
text: I(K) = ker(dim mod 2) on the Witt ring of TauCeti#7604 is generated as an additive group by the one-fold Pfister classes ⟨⟨a⟩⟩ = ⟨1, −a⟩ (Lam, Ch. II §1).

name: Scalar curvature
text: the basis-free metric trace of the Ricci tensor of a connection on a Riemannian tangent bundle, with its orthonormal-basis, Einstein and constant-curvature formulas, n(n − 1)κ when R(w, u)v = κ(⟨u, v⟩w − ⟨w, v⟩u) (Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, Ch. 7).

name: The minimal discriminant ideal
text: 𝔇_{E/K} = ∏ᵥ 𝔭ᵥ^(v(Δ_min,v)) for an elliptic curve over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain O, a finite nonzero product invariant under change of variables, and for an equation integral over O equal to (Δ) exactly when the equation is globally minimal (Silverman VIII.8).

name: Unramified extensions of local fields
text: for an extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, e(L/K) = 1 with separable residue extension (automatic here), shown equivalent to v_L ∘ ι = v_K, to 𝔪_K 𝒪_L = 𝔪_L, to f(L/K) = [L : K], stable in towers in both directions, and identified with Mathlib's `Algebra.FormallyUnramified 𝒪[K] 𝒪[L]` (Serre, *Corps Locaux* I §4, III §5).

name: The Weyl dimension formula
text: for a finite-dimensional module M generated by a highest-weight vector of weight λ over a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, dim M = ∏_{α>0} ⟨λ+ρ, α^∨⟩ / ⟨ρ, α^∨⟩, specialised from the Weyl character formula of TauCeti#7644 (Humphreys §24.3); the statement for L(λ) at every dominant integral λ still waits on the injectivity half of PBW.

name: The first Bianchi identity
text: R(u,v)w + R(v,w)u + R(w,u)v = 0 for the curvature of any torsion-free smooth connection on the tangent bundle, in any finite dimension, boundary allowed, no metric needed (Lee, *Riemannian Manifolds*, Ch. 7).

name: The functional equation of a newform, with its sign
text: for a newform f of weight k and trivial nebentypus, Λ_N(k − s, f) = i^k ε_N(f) Λ_N(s, f) with ε_N(f) the Fricke sign, the two-form Fricke equation announced earlier collapsed to one form; the sign i^k ε_N(f) is ±1, and when it is −1 the L-function vanishes at s = k/2, so the analytic rank is positive (Diamond–Shurman Thm 5.10.2).

name: 𝔸_K/K is compact
text: for a number field K the quotient of the adele ring by the diagonal copy of K is compact, via a compact set of representatives from strong approximation and the Minkowski parallelepiped (Cassels–Fröhlich II §14); the adeles, ideles and idele class group are now locally compact Hausdorff as well.

name: A simultaneous Petersson-orthonormal Hecke eigenbasis
text: every fixed-nebentypus cusp space S_k(N, χ) has a finite basis, orthonormal for the Petersson product, whose vectors are eigenforms for every T_n with gcd(n, N) = 1, resting on the good T_n being normal with Petersson adjoint ⟨n⟩⁻¹T_n (Diamond–Shurman Thm 5.5.4).

name: The decomposition group is the local Galois group
text: for L/K Galois and a place w of L over a finite place v of K, continuous extension to the completions is an isomorphism D_w ≅ Gal(L_w/K_v), so L_w/K_v is Galois, cyclic of order f when w is unramified, and the global arithmetic Frobenius at w extends to the local one (Neukirch II §9); locally, reduction gives Gal(L/K) ≅ Gal(𝓀_L/𝓀_K) for unramified extensions of local fields.

name: The adic spectrum of A⟨T/s⟩ is the rational subset
text: for a Huber ring A, pullback along A → A⟨T/s⟩ is a homeomorphism Spa(A⟨T/s⟩, A_U⁺) ≃ R(T/s) (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Prop. 8.2(2), first assertion), built on Spa(Â, Â⁺) ≃ Spa(A, A⁺) for the completion, matching rational subsets (Prop. 7.48, TauCeti#7848, TauCeti#7913); the two-piece Laurent case of Tate acyclicity (Lemma 8.33) landed alongside.

name: The small-chains theorem
text: for an open cover U of a space X, the inclusion of the singular chains subordinate to U into all singular chains is a chain homotopy equivalence with a strict retraction, hence an isomorphism on singular homology (Hatcher Prop. 2.21), the input to excision.

name: The Galois correspondence for normal extensions
text: for E/F normal but not necessarily separable, Gal(E/F) is profinite and its closed subgroups correspond to the intermediate fields of the separable closure of F in E. Mathlib has the infinite Galois correspondence for Galois extensions; this is its extension to imperfect base fields, which also makes the absolute Galois group profinite.

name: H² regularity of whole-space weak solutions
text: for a constant uniformly elliptic matrix A, a weak solution u ∈ H¹(ℝⁿ) of −∂ⱼ(Aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) = f with f ∈ L² lies in H²(ℝⁿ), with ‖∂_w∂_y u‖_{L²} ≤ ‖y‖‖w‖‖f‖_{L²}/λ, by difference quotients (Evans §6.3.1 Thm 1); interior estimates and variable coefficients are the next steps.

name: Local monogenicity
text: a discrete valuation ring S, finite over a discrete valuation subring R with separable residue extension, is R[β] for a single β, with the resulting integral power basis (Serre, *Corps Locaux* III §6 Prop. 12); Mathlib has the unramified case, and this covers tame and wild ramification without assuming completeness.

name: Type II codes have length divisible by eight
text: a doubly-even self-dual binary code has 8 ∣ n, from the MacWilliams identity and the symmetry W(X, iY) = W(X, Y) of its weight enumerator (Huffman–Pless Ch. 9).

name: The primitive quadratic character of a fundamental discriminant
text: a fundamental discriminant D defines a Dirichlet character of level |D|, the product of the characters of its prime discriminants; it is primitive and equals the Legendre symbol (D/q) at every odd prime q (Ireland–Rosen Ch. 6).

name: The chain rule and truncation in W^{1,p}(Ω)
text: for Lipschitz C¹ F with F(0) = 0, F ∘ u ∈ W^{1,p} with ∇(F ∘ u) = F′(u)∇u, and u⁺ ∈ W^{1,p} with ∇u⁺ = 1_{u>0}∇u (Gilbarg–Trudinger Lemma 7.6); the Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality, announced earlier for C¹ functions, now holds on W^{1,p}(Ω) for bounded convex Ω with the same constant.

name: Differential graded categories
text: categories enriched in cochain complexes of R-modules, with the homogeneous-morphism calculus and the graded Leibniz rule d(fg) = (df)g + (−1)^{|f|} f(dg), compared with Mathlib's Hom complexes of cochain complexes (Keller, *Deriving DG categories*); the DG Yoneda lemma for the free rank-one right module came with it.

name: The free profinite group
text: the profinite completion of the free group on a type X, with its universal property, that a map from X into a profinite group extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism; functorial in X and unique up to unique isomorphism (Ribes–Zalesskii Ch. 3).

name: The two-dimensional Ginzburg DG algebra
text: Π₂(Q) for a finite quiver Q: the doubled path algebra with a degree −1 loop t_i at each vertex and d(t_i) the preprojective relator ρ_i, with d² = 0 and bidegree (1, 0) (Ginzburg, *Calabi–Yau algebras* §4.2; Keller, *Deformed Calabi–Yau completions* §6.5); H⁰(Π₂(Q)) ≅ Π(Q) is the next step.

name: Pic⁰ of a curve
text: on a proper integral curve, the Euler-characteristic degree deg L = χ(L) − χ(𝒪_X) is a homomorphism Pic X → ℤ, its kernel Pic⁰ X is degree-zero divisors modulo principal divisors, and a point of residue degree one gives Pic X / Pic⁰ X ≅ ℤ (Hartshorne II.6, IV.1).

name: The Chebotarev density theorem

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#9071, TauCeti#9160, TauCeti#9074, TauCeti#9039, TauCeti#8276, TauCeti#9295, TauCeti#8380

text: for a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields and a conjugacy class C of G = Gal(L/K), the primes of K with Frobenius in C have Dirichlet and natural density #C/#G among all primes of K, with π_C(x) ~ (#C/#G)·Li(x), via a cyclotomic crossing and Wiener–Ikehara (Neukirch VII §13); the prime ideal theorem π_K(x) ~ Li(x) is now unconditional for every number field, as is density 1/φ(m) for primes in each invertible class mod m.

name: Excision and Mayer–Vietoris for singular homology
text: when the interiors of A and B cover X, (A, A ∩ B) → (X, B) is an isomorphism on relative singular homology, and an open cover X = U ∪ V gives the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence, with coefficients in any abelian category with coproducts (Hatcher 2.20, §2.2); singular cohomology with its long exact sequence and homotopy invariance follows.

name: The Hopf–Rinow theorem
text: for a Riemannian manifold M with its Riemannian distance, the following are equivalent: exp_p is defined on all of T_pM, M is proper, M is complete, M is geodesically complete; each gives a minimizing geodesic from p to every point, so complete manifolds are geodesic spaces and compact ones are geodesically complete (do Carmo VII 2.8).

name: Serre duality for divisor sheaves on a curve
text: H¹(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨ ≅ H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(K − D)) for a proper integral curve X over k, with DVR local rings at codimension-one points and k integrally closed in k(X), and K a canonical divisor, through Weil's repartitions (Serre, AGCF II §5), with deg K = 2g − 2; H¹(X, 𝒪_X) is now proved finite-dimensional, making the Riemann–Roch theorem announced earlier unconditional.

name: Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality
text: for probability measures with finite first moment on a Polish space, W₁(μ, ν) = sup ∫f dμ − ∫f dν over 1-Lipschitz f (Villani, Topics, 1.14); on ℝ, W_p is the L^p(0,1) distance of the quantile functions for all 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, the monotone coupling being optimal, and for p < ∞ empirical measures of an i.i.d. sample with finite p-th moment converge almost surely in W_p.

name: Lovász–Szegedy compactness of graphon space

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#8837, TauCeti#9072, TauCeti#9199, TauCeti#8687, TauCeti#9174, TauCeti#8382

text: graphons on [0,1] modulo cut distance form a compact metric space (Lovász–Szegedy 2007); a graph parameter is a homomorphism density t(·, W) iff it is isomorphism-invariant, multiplicative, normalized and reflection positive; cut-distance convergence is convergence of all homomorphism densities; and probability measures on graphon space correspond to exchangeable random graphs (Diaconis–Janson; TauCeti#8687, TauCeti#9174).

name: The Lie–Kolchin theorem
text: every finite-dimensional representation of a connected solvable reduced affine algebraic group of finite type over an algebraically closed field is upper triangularizable (Humphreys §17.6); hence the Borel subgroups of GLₙ are exactly the conjugates of the upper-triangular group.

name: Newforms are an orthogonal basis of the new subspace
text: the newforms of level N and weight k are a Petersson-orthogonal basis of S_k(Γ₁(N))^new (Diamond–Shurman 5.8.2), the g(dτ) for newforms g of level M with dM | N span S_k(Γ₁(N)) (5.8.3, spanning half; TauCeti#9038), and a newform of trivial nebentypus has Atkin–Lehner signs ε_Q(f) = ±1 for Q ∥ N multiplying to its Fricke sign.

name: The Schwarz–Christoffel theorem for polygonal Jordan domains
text: a bounded domain with Jordan-curve frontier, locally a half-plane away from finitely many vertices and a sector of opening (eᵢ + 1)π at each, is the image of the upper half-plane under A·F + B, F the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive, prevertices going to vertices (Ahlfors VI §2); the convex case announced earlier now covers reentrant polygons, using that a simple arc does not separate the plane and a separating Jordan curve bounds each complementary component.

name: Serre's theorem on pro-p groups of cohomological dimension one
text: a pro-p group with cd_p ≤ 1, equivalently a projective one, is free pro-p: on a pointed profinite space in general, and of rank d(G) when topologically finitely generated; H²(F, M) = 0 for free pro-p F is TauCeti#8533 (Serre, Galois Cohomology I §4.2).

name: The Murnaghan–Nakayama rule for Schur polynomials
text: p_r · s_ν = Σ_μ (−1)^{ht(μ/ν)} s_μ over the μ with μ/ν a rim hook of r cells, over any commutative ring, in symmetric-function form (Macdonald I.3 Ex. 11), with Jacobi's bialternant formula s_μ · a_δ = a_{λ+δ} as input.

name: Sₙ is a Galois group over ℚ in every degree
text: for every n ≥ 1 some monic integer polynomial of degree n, irreducible over ℚ, has Galois group Sₙ, via reductions mod 2, 3 and 5 (van der Waerden §61); the Galois group of a quartic is read off discriminant and resolvent cubic, that of a quintic off Dummit's sextic resolvent.

name: Jordan's theorem for a cycle of prime length
text: a primitive permutation group of degree n containing a p-cycle, p prime with p + 3 ≤ n, contains the alternating group (Wielandt 13.9); the transposition and 3-cycle cases are Mathlib's.

name: Harnack's inequality in every dimension
text: for K compact in a preconnected open U ⊆ ℝⁿ there is C with u(x) ≤ C·u(y) on K for every nonnegative harmonic u on U, from the mean-value property on spheres and balls in ℝⁿ, which Mathlib has only in the plane; the planar disk case was announced earlier (Gilbarg–Trudinger 2.5).

name: Hilbert's formula for the different exponent
text: for a finite Galois extension L/K of local fields with lower ramification groups Gᵢ, d(L/K) = Σᵢ≥0 (#Gᵢ − 1) (Serre, Corps Locaux IV §1), alongside d = e − 1 iff L/K is tame and the Herbrand function φ_{L/K} with the upper numbering.

name: Existence of globally minimal Weierstrass equations
text: over a Dedekind domain an elliptic curve has a globally minimal equation iff its Weierstrass class is trivial, so every elliptic curve over ℚ has one over ℤ, unique in Cremona's reduced form (Silverman VIII.8.2–8.3); also E[N] ≅ ℤ/N × ℤ/N over a separably closed field with N invertible.

name: Weierstrass preparation for restricted power series
text: over a complete nonarchimedean field, a power series restricted to the closed disc of radius c and distinguished of degree s is uniquely a unit of the restricted ring times a monic polynomial of degree s (BGR 5.2.2), the Tate-algebra form, distinct from Mathlib's theorem over I-adically complete rings.

name: The weak maximum principle for divergence-form elliptic equations
text: for −div(a∇u) + b·∇u + cu with bounded measurable coefficients, uniform ellipticity, c ≥ 0 and small drift, a weak subsolution with positive part in W₀^{1,2}(Ω) is nonpositive a.e., with the comparison principle (Gilbarg–Trudinger 8.1); also interior H² regularity for constant coefficients and local Rellich–Kondrachov compactness.

name: Cartier divisors and the Picard group of an integral scheme
text: on an integral scheme, without Noetherian hypotheses, every line bundle is 𝒪_X(D) for a Cartier divisor D, 𝒪_X(D) is trivial iff D is principal, and 𝒪_X(D) ⊗ 𝒪_X(E) ≅ 𝒪_X(D + E) (Hartshorne II.6.13–6.15).

name: Atomless standard Borel probability spaces are the unit interval mod 0
text: an atomless standard Borel probability space is isomorphic mod null sets to ([0,1], Lebesgue), via the distribution function and its quantile (Janson A.7).

name: Free groups are residually p
text: for every prime p, every nontrivial element of a free group survives in a finite p-group quotient (Magnus, Iwasawa), so free groups embed in the free pro-p group.

name: The compactified quotient of a Fuchsian group is a Riemann surface
text: for discrete Γ ≤ PSL(2,ℝ), Γ\ℍ with its cusp orbits adjoined has a holomorphic atlas of elliptic and q-coordinate cusp charts (Diamond–Shurman §2.4); a cofinite group has finitely many cusp orbits and X(1) is compact, compactness for general cofinite Γ still open.

name: Regular local rings are domains
text: a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal has dim R generators is a domain, and a DVR exactly in dimension one (Stacks 00NP); schemes smooth over a regular locally Noetherian scheme have regular local rings.

name: The norm-one idele class group is compact
text: for a number field K the kernel C_K¹ of the idele class norm is compact, the adelic form of class-group finiteness and Dirichlet's unit theorem, which the proof consumes (Cassels–Fröhlich II §16).

name: Quadratic forms of rank at most three are classified by discriminant and Hasse invariant
text: for regular forms of fixed rank ≤ 3 over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, with s(q) = ∏_{i<j} (aᵢ, aⱼ) ∈ Br(K) (Lam V.3.21); the signed discriminant gives I(K)/I(K)² ≅ Kˣ/(Kˣ)², and a two-fold Pfister form is isotropic iff hyperbolic iff its quaternion algebra splits.

name: Gordan's and Stiemke's theorems of the alternative
text: over any linearly ordered field, either some functional is strictly positive on a finite family of vectors or the family has a nontrivial nonnegative relation, and a subspace of Kⁿ has no nonzero nonnegative vector iff a strictly positive vector is orthogonal to it (Schrijver Ch. 7); Mathlib's Farkas lemma is over ℝ.

name: Symplectic bases, and Albert's theorem in characteristic two
text: a nondegenerate alternating form over any field has a basis with matrix J (Artin 3.7), and a symmetric bilinear form has an orthogonal basis iff it is zero or not alternating, in every characteristic (Albert 1938; TauCeti#8437).

name: Finite-quotient determinacy of profinite groups
text: a topologically finitely generated profinite group is determined up to topological isomorphism by its continuous finite quotients (Dixon–Formanek–Poland–Ribes 1982); finitely generated groups with the same finite quotients have isomorphic profinite completions.

name: Tate's cohomological triviality criterion
text: for a finite group G, a G-module whose cohomology vanishes in two consecutive degrees on every subgroup of prime-power order has vanishing Tate cohomology in every degree on every subgroup (Milne, CFT II 3.10); inflation–restriction is exact in every positive degree under the usual vanishing hypotheses.

name: Continuous H² classifies profinite extensions
text: for a profinite group G acting continuously on a profinite abelian group M, profinite extensions of G by M modulo continuous equivalence correspond to continuous-cochain H²(G, M), the zero class being the continuously split ones (Ribes–Zalesskii Ch. 6).

name: The Schur multiplier is finite
text: for a finite group G and an algebraically closed field k of any characteristic, H²(G, kˣ) is finite, every class having a factor set valued in the |G|-th roots of unity (Karpilovsky); in characteristic p this is the p′-part of the integral multiplier.

name: The exchange condition for the Weyl group of a Tits system
text: in a Tits system, if s is a simple reflection and ℓ(sw) < ℓ(w) with w = s₁⋯s_q, then sw is the same word with one letter deleted (Bourbaki IV §2 Thm 2, without the Coxeter conclusion); the Bruhat cells BwB are pairwise disjoint.

name: K₀ of an abelian category is K₀ of its bounded derived category
text: K₀(A) ≅ K₀(Dᵇ(A)) for an essentially small abelian category, the inverse being the alternating sum of cohomology (Weibel, K-book II Ex. 9.15); split K₀ of an additive category is K₀ of its bounded homotopy category, and K₀(proj A), G₀(mod A) and the Cartan map are Morita invariant.

name: Preprojective algebras of non-Dynkin graphs are infinite-dimensional
text: for every orientation of a connected non-Dynkin graph the preprojective algebra is infinite-dimensional over every field (Ringel; the non-Dynkin direction only), via a Golod–Shafarevich-type bound.

name: The symmetric power of a complex curve is a complex manifold
text: Symⁿ of a Hausdorff Riemann surface is a complex manifold with elementary-symmetric charts, analytic also at colliding points (Ozsváth–Szabó §2.2).

name: Polarizable rational Hodge structures form a semisimple abelian category
text: polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight n form an abelian category in which every object is a finite biproduct of simple ones (Voisin I §7.1.2); effective weight-one integral Hodge structures on a lattice are the complex structures on its realification, polarizations being Riemann forms.

name: The Riemannian volume measure
text: a continuous Riemannian metric, boundary and corners allowed and no orientation needed, determines a locally finite Borel measure glued from the chart densities √det g (Lee 2.44), invariant under isometries.

name: Hurwitz class numbers count classes of binary quadratic forms
text: for D > 0, H(D) is the sum over SL₂(ℤ)-classes of positive definite integral forms of discriminant −D of 2/|Stab|, each class containing exactly one reduced form (Cohen §5.3).

name: Hecke characters
text: continuous characters C_K → ℂˣ of the idele class group of a number field; the finite-order ones are exactly the pullbacks of ray class characters.

name: The Tate curve over ℤ⟦q⟧
text: y² + xy = x³ + a₄(q)x + a₆(q) with a₄ = −5Σσ₃(n)qⁿ and 12a₆ = −Σ(5σ₃(n) + 7σ₅(n))qⁿ over ℤ⟦q⟧, with Δ = q − 24q² + ⋯ and j = q⁻¹ + 744 + ⋯, nodal at q = 0 (Silverman, Advanced Topics V §3).

name: Brauer's induction theorem
text: for a finite group G over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every virtual character is a ℤ-linear combination of characters induced from elementary subgroups (products of a cyclic group and a p-group), so the direct sum of the induction maps from elementary subgroups is surjective onto the virtual characters; Artin's rational form was TauCeti#2258 (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, Ch. 10).

name: Gabriel's theorem, completed to the positive-root bijection
text: for a finite quiver with positive definite Tits form, over any field, every nonnegative integer vector of Tits norm 1 is the dimension vector of a finite-dimensional indecomposable representation, by running the Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev reflection functors backwards; with the uniqueness half of TauCeti#5299 this makes the dimension vector a bijection from isomorphism classes of indecomposables to positive roots, D₄ having 12 classes; the ADE classification of the positive-definite quivers is still open (BGP 1973).

name: Every ordered field has a real closure
text: an ordered algebraic extension which is real closed, by Zorn on preorderings (existence only; uniqueness is not yet done); for a real closed field R, [R(√−1) is algebraically closed](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/RealClosure/AlgebraicClosed.html#TauCeti.RealClosure.isAlgClosed_quadraticAlgebra), so irreducible polynomials over R have degree at most two, and the [polynomial intermediate value theorem](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/RealClosure/IVT.html#Polynomial.exists_root_Ioo) and Rolle's theorem hold over every real closed field, Archimedean or not; Mathlib master has the class `IsRealClosed` with its basic square and odd-degree-root lemmas (Artin–Schreier 1927; Bochnak–Coste–Roy Ch. 1).

name: The irreducible characters of GL₂(𝔽_q)
text: the q−1 linear characters α∘det, the q−1 Steinberg twists, the (q−1)(q−2)/2 principal series Ind_B(α⊗β) with α ≠ β and the q(q−1)/2 cuspidal characters attached to θ : 𝔽_{q²}ˣ → ℂˣ with θ^q ≠ θ are pairwise distinct and exhaust the irreducible complex characters, their number being the class number q² − 1; the [cuspidal representation](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/GL2/Cuspidal/Irreducible.html#TauCeti.GL2Cuspidal) is constructed as a simple representation of degree q − 1 (Fulton–Harris §5.2; Piatetski-Shapiro §§4–5).

name: The pro-p Nielsen–Schreier theorem

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#9498, TauCeti#9205, TauCeti#9608, TauCeti#9270, TauCeti#9641, TauCeti#9630

text: every closed subgroup of a free pro-p group, on any set of generators, is free pro-p on a basis converging to 1, through cd_p(free) ≤ 1 and Serre's theorem of TauCeti#9205; an [open subgroup of index m in a free pro-p group of finite rank n ≥ 1 is free pro-p of rank 1 + m(n − 1)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Free/OpenSubgroup.html#TauCeti.freeProP.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_freeProP_openSubgroup_index), the Schreier index formula, from the two-term Euler characteristic formula, and the cardinality of a basis converging to 1 is an invariant (Serre, *Galois Cohomology* I §4.2; Ribes–Zalesskii 7.7.5).

name: The homology of spheres
text: the reduced singular homology of the unit sphere of an (n+1)-dimensional real inner product space is one copy of the coefficient object in degree n and zero in every other degree, with coefficients in any abelian category with coproducts, by induction through the suspension isomorphism; hence [H_k(Dⁿ, Sⁿ⁻¹)](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/DiskSphere.html#TauCeti.singularHomologyDiskBoundaryPairIso) is R for k = n and zero otherwise, for every n including n = 0 (Hatcher 2.14); Mathlib master has singular homology with H₀ and homotopy invariance but no sphere computation.

name: Herbrand's theorem
text: for a finite Galois extension M/K of nonarchimedean local fields and a Galois subextension L/K with H = Gal(M/L), the lower ramification groups satisfy (G/H)_{φ_{M/L}(u)} = G_u H/H for all real u ≥ −1, from Serre's lower index i_G and his quotient formula e(M/L)·i_{L/K}(σ') = Σ_{σ|_L = σ'} i_{M/K}(σ), and the Herbrand function carries the lower jumps to the upper jumps; transitivity of φ and the upper-numbering form (G/H)^v = G^v H/H are the next steps (Serre, *Corps Locaux* IV §3).

name: Existence and uniqueness of unramified extensions of local fields
text: inside an algebraic closure of a nonarchimedean local field K with residue field of order q, the splitting field of X^{q^f} − X, equivalently K(ζ_{q^f−1}), is the unique unramified subextension of degree f for every f ≥ 1; their union is the [maximal unramified extension K^ur](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Unramified/Maximal.html#TauCeti.maximalUnramifiedFrobenius), Galois over K, whose arithmetic Frobenius is a topological generator of Gal(K^ur/K), the identification with Ẑ being the next step; unramifiedness, defined in TauCeti#7813, is also shown stable under base change and composita and equivalent to étaleness of 𝒪_L over 𝒪_K (Serre, *Corps Locaux* III §5).

name: The subword property of Bruhat order
text: in any Coxeter system, u ≤ w in the Bruhat order of TauCeti#5472 exactly when some subword of a fixed reduced word for w spells u; the new direction is that every subword of a reduced word lies below the whole word, by the right-multiplication lifting property (Björner–Brenti 2.2.2).

name: The first variation of energy
text: for a C² variation F of a curve γ in a Riemannian manifold, d/ds E(F_s)|_{s=0} = ⟨V(b), γ'(b)⟩ − ⟨V(a), γ'(a)⟩ − ∫_a^b ⟨V, D_t γ'⟩ dt with V the variation field and D_t the Levi-Civita derivative, so [geodesics are critical points of the energy](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/Geodesic/FirstVariation.html#TauCeti.Manifold.IsGeodesicCurveOn.hasDerivAt_energy_zero) among fixed-endpoint variations; the converse, that critical curves are geodesics, is not yet done (do Carmo IX 2.4; Milnor, *Morse Theory* §12).

name: The Hilbert symbol is nondegenerate in odd residue characteristic
text: over a nonarchimedean local field in which 2 is a unit of 𝒪_K, the norms from K(√a) have index two in Kˣ for every nonsquare a, so the symbol of TauCeti#7286 is bimultiplicative and every nonsquare a has some b with (a, b) = −1, with [Serre's closed formula](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/QuadraticForm/OddResidue/Formula.html#TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_oddResidue_formula) (π^α u, π^β v) = ((−1)^{(q−1)/2})^{αβ} ε(u)^β ε(v)^α for ε the residue quadratic character and the resulting local Hasse invariant on isometry classes of quadratic forms; the dyadic case is still open (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic* III §1).

name: Newforms are eigenforms for every Hecke operator
text: a newform f of level N satisfies U_p f = a_p(f) f at every prime p dividing N, hence T_n f = a_n(f) f for all n ≥ 1 with the Fourier coefficients as eigenvalues, proved through strong multiplicity one rather than through U_p-stability of the new subspace; this is the bad-prime eigenvalue theorem left open when newforms were announced in TauCeti#6261 (Atkin–Lehner; Diamond–Shurman 5.8.2; Miyake 4.6.13).

name: Tate's isomorphism criterion
text: for a finite group G and a morphism f : A → B of G-modules, if on every subgroup of prime-power order f is surjective on Tate cohomology in degree q − 1, bijective in degree q and injective in degree q + 1, then f is an isomorphism on Ĥⁿ(S, ·) for every integer n and every subgroup S, by the triviality criterion of TauCeti#9140; with the Artin–Tate splitting module and the degree-zero cup criterion this is the input to Tate's theorem for class formations, not yet assembled (Artin–Tate, Prelim. §2 Thm A; Cassels–Fröhlich IV §10).

name: The Frobenius characteristic map
text: the linear isomorphism from class functions on Sₙ to homogeneous symmetric polynomials of degree n in d ≥ n variables sending the character of the Specht module S^μ to the Schur polynomial s_μ, the Schur coefficients of a class function being its pairings with the Specht characters; the power-sum formula p_ρ = Σ_λ χ^λ(ρ) s_λ is the next step (Macdonald I §7).

name: The Maslov index
text: for a loop of maximal totally real subspaces of a finite-dimensional complex vector space, the degree in the circle of its loop of Maslov phases: independent of the reference subspace, computed from the determinant of a frame, invariant under homotopy of loops, and equal to n on the half-turn t ↦ e^{iπt} L₀ of an n-dimensional subspace, with the degree of a loop in S¹ defined by covering-space lifting and matched with π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ (McDuff–Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves*, App. C.3).

name: The Legendre–Fenchel conjugate and the subdifferential
text: on a real dual pair, f*(y) = sup_x (⟨x, y⟩ − f(x)) for extended-real f, with the Fenchel–Young inequality, the Galois connection between conjugation on the two sides, f** ≤ f and f*** = f*, and convexity and lower semicontinuity of every conjugate; the [subdifferential](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/Subdifferential.html#TauCeti.subdifferential) ∂f(x), characterized by equality in Fenchel–Young, convex and closed, with y ∈ ∂f(x) implying x ∈ ∂f*(y); Fenchel–Moreau is the next step (Rockafellar, *Convex Analysis*, §§12, 23).

name: Sectional curvature
text: K(u, v) = ⟨R(u, v)v, u⟩ / det Gram(u, v) for the curvature tensor of a metric-compatible covariant derivative, specialized to the Levi-Civita connection, with the constant-curvature predicates and the proof that R(u, v)w = κ(⟨v, w⟩u − ⟨u, w⟩v) has sectional curvature κ; a bundled complete hyperbolic metric of curvature −1 follows (Lee, *Riemannian Manifolds*, Ch. 8).

name: Demushkin groups
text: a pro-p group with H¹(G, 𝔽_p) finite-dimensional, H²(G, 𝔽_p) one-dimensional and the cup product H¹ × H¹ → H² nondegenerate; such a group is finitely generated and one-relator with relator in F^p[F, F], ℤ/2 is Demushkin at p = 2, a Demushkin group at an odd prime has even rank, free pro-p groups are not Demushkin, and a one-relator pro-p group on n generators has abelianization ℤ_p^{n−1} × ℤ_p/q; Labute's classification is the target (Labute 1967; Serre, *Galois Cohomology* I §4.5).

name: The Green function and Poisson kernel of the unit ball in ℝⁿ
text: the Dirichlet Green kernel by the method of images, symmetric, harmonic in y away from the pole and vanishing on the sphere, and the Poisson kernel (1 − |x|²)/(n ωₙ |x − y|ⁿ) as minus its outward normal derivative on the sphere, for n ≠ 2, the planar disk having its logarithmic kernel matched with Mathlib's Poisson kernel in TauCeti#9283; the Poisson integral theorem is the next step (Evans §2.2.4).

name: The Aldous–Hoover representation for separately exchangeable arrays
text: a random array (X_{ij})_{i,j ∈ ℕ} in a standard Borel space is separately exchangeable, its law invariant under independent permutations of the rows and of the columns, exactly when it has the law of X_{ij} = F(U, U_i, V_j, U_{ij}) for one measurable F and independent uniform variables attached to the whole array, to each row, to each column and to each cell; this is the summit of the array work announced earlier, and the jointly exchangeable representation is still open (Aldous 1981; Hoover 1979; Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).

name: The Sturm–Tarski theorem over real closed fields
text: over any real closed ordered field, not only ℝ, if a < b are not roots of p and the roots of p in (a, b) are simple, the drop in sign variations of the signed remainder sequence of p and f·p′ from a to b is the sum of the signs of f at those roots, Sturm's root count being the case f = 1, with half-line and whole-line forms; alongside it, [Thom's lemma](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/Thom.html#Polynomial.thomEncoding_injOn): the signs of the successive derivatives of a nonzero polynomial at its roots identify each root and determine their order, multiple roots allowed; Mathlib master has the Sturm sequence but not the theorem (Basu–Pollack–Roy, *Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry*, §2.2).

name: Finite local Galois groups are solvable
text: for a finite extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, Aut(L/K) is solvable through its ramification filtration 1 ⊴ G₁ ⊴ G₀ ⊴ G, with G/G₀ and G₀/G₁ cyclic and wild inertia G₁ a p-group, the embeddings G_i/G_{i+1} ↪ U_i/U_{i+1} now being injective without a monogenic generator (Serre, *Corps Locaux* IV §2); separately, [Gal(K^ur/K) ≅ Ẑ](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Unramified/ZHat.html#TauCeti.maximalUnramifiedGaloisGroupEquivZHat) with arithmetic Frobenius going to 1, the step named when unramified extensions were announced, and the [inertia subgroup](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Unramified/Inertia.html#TauCeti.inertiaSubgroup) I_K of the absolute Galois group is closed and normal with 1 → I_K → G_K → Gal(K^ur/K) → 1 exact and the arithmetic Frobenius lifts forming one coset of I_K (Serre, *Corps Locaux* III §5).

name: The Weil pairing
text: for an elliptic curve E over a separably closed field F and N invertible in F, e_N(S, T) = τ_S g_T / g_T, where div g_T = [N]*(T) − [N]*(O) and τ_S is translation by S, is a well-defined pairing E[N] × E[N] → μ_N(F), additive in each variable and [nondegenerate in the second](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/MulByInt/WeilPairing.html#TauCeti.Isogeny.eq_zero_of_forall_weilPairing_eq_zero), built on a general Kummer character σ ↦ σα/α; e_N(T, T) = 1, Galois equivariance and non-closed base fields are not yet done (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.8).

name: The basic perturbation lemma
text: for a special contraction (i, p, h) of a module with endomorphism d_M onto one with d_N, and a perturbation δ with 1 + δh invertible (for instance δh locally nilpotent), setting X = (1 + δh)⁻¹δ, the maps i − hXi, p − pXh and h − hXh form a special contraction of (M, d_M + δ) onto (N, d_N + pXi), with (d_N + pXi)² = d_N²; its intended use, homotopy transfer of A∞-structures along bar constructions, is not yet done (E. H. Brown 1959; Gugenheim–Lambe–Stasheff; Crainic, *On the perturbation lemma, and deformations*).

name: Dedekind's non-monogenic cubic field
text: for K = ℚ(θ) with θ³ − θ² − 2θ − 8 = 0, the prime 2 splits into three distinct primes of residue degree one, more than the two monic linear polynomials over 𝔽₂ can account for, so 2 is a common index divisor and 𝒪_K ≠ ℤ[α] for every α; with [discr K = −503](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/WorkedExamples/DedekindCubic/Invariants.html#TauCeti.NumberField.dedekindCubic_discr_eq_neg_five_hundred_three), θ of index 2 and signature (1, 1) (Dedekind 1878; Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, III §2).

name: The finite triangle groups
text: for 1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ c, the triangle group Δ(a, b, c) = ⟨x, y, z | xᵃ = yᵇ = zᶜ = zyx = 1⟩ is finite exactly when 1/a + 1/b + 1/c > 1, with Δ(2, 3, 3) ≅ A₄, Δ(2, 3, 4) ≅ S₄ and [Δ(2, 3, 5) ≅ A₅](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/GroupTheory/TriangleGroup/Polyhedral.html#TauCeti.TriangleGroup.equivIcosahedral), the order bounds certified by Todd–Coxeter coset tables that the kernel checks (Coxeter–Moser, *Generators and Relations for Discrete Groups*).

name: The sum of squares Σ_{λ ⊢ n} (f^λ)² = n!
text: the squares of the numbers f^λ of standard Young tableaux of the shapes of size n sum to n!, also with f^λ written by the hook-length formula, read off column orthogonality of the character table of Sₙ and dim S^λ = f^λ rather than from the Robinson–Schensted correspondence, which is not formalized (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*; Sagan, *The Symmetric Group*).

name: Modular symbols
text: for Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) and a commutative ring R, 𝕄_w(Γ; R) = (Div⁰(ℙ¹(ℚ)) ⊗ Sym^w(R²))_Γ, with [Manin's lemma](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/ModularSymbols/Basic.html#TauCeti.ModularSymbols.degreeZero_eq_span_unimodular) that Div⁰(ℙ¹(ℚ)) is spanned by the unimodular symbols [g∞] − [g0], finite generation over R for Γ of finite index, and the [Hecke operators](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/ModularSymbols/Hecke.html#TauCeti.ModularSymbols.heckeSymbol) of every double coset, independent of the coset representatives and specializing to T_n on Γ₁(N); commutativity of these operators and the period map to cusp forms are next (Manin 1972; Stein, *Modular Forms: A Computational Approach*, Ch. 8).

name: The mapping cylinder
text: for a continuous f : X → Y, the quotient of I × X ⊔ Y gluing (1, x) to f(x), with its universal property, a strong deformation retraction onto Y making it [homotopy equivalent to Y](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/MappingCylinder.html#TauCeti.MappingCylinder.homotopyEquiv), and X included as a closed cofibration with the [homotopy extension property](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Homotopy/Extension/MappingCylinder.html#TauCeti.MappingCylinder.hasHomotopyExtensionProperty_range_incl), so every map factors as a closed cofibration followed by a homotopy equivalence (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Ch. 0).

name: The Seifert–van Kampen theorem for the fundamental groupoid
text: for any open cover of a topological space X, with no connectedness assumption on the members or their intersections, the fundamental groupoid of X is the colimit, in groupoids, of the fundamental groupoids of the nonempty finite intersections; the existence half is a [gluing](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Glue.html#TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoid.glue) of functors that agree on pairwise intersections; the two-set pushout and the statements for fundamental groups are not yet derived, and a cosheaf formulation is in progress upstream as mathlib4#41603 (Brown, *Topology and Groupoids*, §6.7).

name: Kantorovich duality with dual attainment on Polish spaces
text: for a bounded continuous nonnegative cost c on a product of Polish spaces and probability measures μ, ν, the optimal transport cost is the maximum of ∫φ dμ + ∫ψ dν over integrable φ, ψ with φ(x) + ψ(y) ≤ c(x, y), attained by a c-conjugate pair, where the duality of TauCeti#5069 needed compact spaces and gave a supremum; unbounded and lower semicontinuous costs remain (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 5.10). Alongside, [Rockafellar's theorem](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/CTransform/Rockafellar.html#TauCeti.isCyclicallyMonotone_pairingCost_iff_exists_fenchelConjugate): a subset of a real dual pair is cyclically monotone exactly when it lies in the subdifferential graph of a Legendre–Fenchel conjugate.

name: Tate's theorem for class formations, and abstract Artin reciprocity
text: for a finite normal layer V ◁ U of a class formation A, with Γ = U/V, cup product with the fundamental class is an isomorphism Ĥʳ(Γ, ℤ) ≅ Ĥʳ⁺²(Γ, A^V) in every integer degree r, from a [generic criterion](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Cup/TateTheorem.html#TauCeti.TateCohomology.cup_bijective_of_forall_isPGroup) on the subgroups of prime-power order; degree −2 gives the [reciprocity isomorphism](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Formation/ArtinMap.html#TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation.artinEquiv) A^U / N(A^V) ≅ Γ^ab, so the Artin map is surjective with kernel the norms; this assembles the criterion of TauCeti#9453, and no local or global class formation has been constructed yet (Artin–Tate, *Class Field Theory*, XIV §§4–5).

name: Happel's theorem
text: the stable category of a Frobenius exact category, in which the morphisms factoring through projective-injective objects are set to zero, is triangulated, with shift the stable suspension and distinguished triangles coming from conflations; the octahedral axiom is the new part (Happel, *Triangulated Categories in the Representation Theory of Finite Dimensional Algebras*, I Thm 2.6).

name: Tori over a perfect field are classified by Galois lattices
text: over a perfect field k, sending a torus to its [character lattice](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Torus/CharacterLattice/Equivalence.html#TauCeti.TorusCommHopfAlgCat.characterLatticeFunctor_isEquivalence) with its continuous action of the absolute Galois group is an anti-equivalence between tori over k and continuous integral Galois lattices, and the cocharacter lattice, naturally its ℤ-dual, classifies tori covariantly; this completes the dictionary whose existence half was announced with TauCeti#6576, and imperfect fields remain (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 12.23, Cor. 12.24).

name: Galois crossed products represent every Brauer class
text: for a finite Galois extension L/K and a 2-cocycle c of Gal(L/K) in Lˣ, the [crossed product](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/CrossedProduct/Basic.html#TauCeti.CrossedProduct) ⊕ L·u_σ with u_σ x = σ(x) u_σ and u_σ u_τ = c(σ, τ) u_στ is central simple over K of dimension [L:K]², cohomologous cocycles give isomorphic algebras, [multiplying cocycles multiplies Brauer classes](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/CrossedProduct/TensorProduct.html#TauCeti.BrauerGroup.crossedProductClass_mul), and every class of Br(K) is that of a crossed product over some finite Galois L/K; injectivity, and with it Br(L/K) ≅ H²(Gal(L/K), Lˣ), is not yet proved (Gille–Szamuely §4.4). Separately, the [Clifford algebra of a nondegenerate quadratic form of even dimension](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/CentralSimple.html#CliffordAlgebra.isSimpleRing_of_even_finrank) is central simple in characteristic ≠ 2 (Lam V.2.4; TauCeti#9804).

name: The Euler product of a newform
text: for a newform f of level N, weight k and nebentypus χ, Σ aₙ n^(−s) = ∏_p (1 − a_p p^(−s) + χ(p) p^(k−1−2s))⁻¹ for Re s > k/2 + 1, with χ(p) = 0 at p ∣ N, resting on the bad-prime eigenvalue theorem of TauCeti#9474 (Diamond–Shurman §5.9); and [a_p(f) = 0 when p² ∣ N and χ is defined modulo N/p](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/BadPrime/Vanishing.html#HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.qExpansion_coeff_prime_eq_zero_of_sq_dvd) (Atkin–Lehner, Li; Miyake 4.6.17; TauCeti#9970).

name: The Hilbert symbol is bimultiplicative and nondegenerate over every local field, dyadic fields included
text: over a nonarchimedean local field K with 2 ≠ 0, in any residue characteristic, the norms from K(√a) have index two in Kˣ for every nonsquare a, by a count of square classes, so (a, bc) = (a, b)(a, c) and every nonsquare a has some b with (a, b) = −1; this removes the odd-residue restriction of TauCeti#9114. The [Hasse invariant](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/QuadraticForm/Hasse.html#TauCeti.RegularFormClass.localHasse) ∏_{i<j} (aᵢ, aⱼ) is then defined on isometry classes in every residue characteristic, and for n ≥ 1 a triple [(n, d, s) is the rank, discriminant and Hasse invariant of a regular form](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/QuadraticForm/Realization.html#TauCeti.RegularFormClass.exists_rank_eq_discr_eq_localHasse_eq_iff) exactly when it is neither (1, d, −1) nor (2, [−1], −1) (TauCeti#10153; Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, IV Prop. 6).

name: Krull–Schmidt cancellation over complete local rings
text: for a complete Noetherian local ring R and an R-algebra A, an indecomposable A-module finitely generated over R has a [local endomorphism ring](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullSchmidt/AdicComplete.html#TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable_of_isAdicComplete), so M ⊕ P ≅ N ⊕ P implies M ≅ N whenever P is finitely generated over R, with no condition on M and N; in particular [finitely generated ℤ_p[G]-modules cancel](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Padics/GroupAlgebra/Cancellation.html#TauCeti.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_prod_linearEquiv) for G finite, beyond the finite-length setting of the Krull–Schmidt theorem of TauCeti#2082 (Curtis–Reiner §6; Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg 5.6.10).

name: The genus of y² = f(x)
text: over a field k with 2 ≠ 0, for squarefree f of degree m ≥ 1 the function field k(x, y) with y² = f(x) has degree 2 over k(x), exact constant field k, ramified places exactly those over the zeros of f together with ∞ when m is odd, and genus ⌊(m − 1)/2⌋, by the Hurwitz genus formula of TauCeti#7306 (Stichtenoth, Ex. 3.7.6, Prop. 6.2.3).

name: The wild bound in Dedekind's different theorem
text: for a finite separable extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields with ramification index e nonzero in L, the different exponent satisfies d(L/K) ≤ e − 1 + v_L(e), so e ≤ d ≤ e − 1 + v_L(e) when the ramification is wild, with the [same bound at every prime of an extension of number fields](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/LocalGlobal/Different/Wild.html#IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.multiplicity_differentIdeal_le_ramificationIdx_sub_one_add_multiplicity_span); on the way, [L/K is totally ramified exactly when 𝒪_L = 𝒪_K[π] for a root π of an Eisenstein polynomial](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Eisenstein/TotallyRamified.html#TauCeti.isTotallyRamified_iff_exists_eisenstein_generator), and a [totally and tamely ramified extension of degree e is K(α) with αᵉ a uniformizer of K](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/TamelyRamified.html#TauCeti.IsTotallyRamified.exists_pow_eq_uniformizer_of_isTamelyRamified) (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, I §6, III §6).

name: The degree of a holomorphic map between compact Riemann surfaces
text: a nonconstant holomorphic map f : X → Y with X compact and connected and Y connected has finite fibres, and the sum of its local multiplicities over a fibre is the same positive number deg f at every point of Y, so f is surjective, and [deg(g ∘ f) = deg g · deg f](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/RiemannSurface/Degree.html#TauCeti.RiemannSurface.degree_comp); with the [open mapping theorem](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/RiemannSurface/OpenMapping.html#TauCeti.RiemannSurface.isOpenMap_of_forall_not_eventuallyConst) and the identity theorem for Riemann surfaces; that degree one forces a biholomorphism is not yet proved (Forster, *Lectures on Riemann Surfaces*, 1.11, 2.7, 4.24).

name: The canonical character of a Demushkin group
text: a Demushkin group G has exactly one continuous character χ : G → ℤ_pˣ with the prescription property, that H¹(G, ℤ_p(χ)/pⁱ) → H¹(G, ℤ_p(χ)/p) is surjective for every i ≥ 1, proved for all p at once by a p-adic Newton iteration on the relator (Labute, Thm 4); every pair (n, A) on Labute's list is [realized](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/NormalForm/Existence.html#TauCeti.exists_isDemushkin_range_eq_of_even_of_lt) as the rank and the image of χ of an explicit one-relator group such as ⟨x₁, …, xₙ | x₁^q (x₁, x₂) ⋯ (xₙ₋₁, xₙ)⟩, and [two Demushkin groups at an odd prime with invariant q = p and the same rank are isomorphic](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/NormalForm/Uniqueness.html#TauCeti.IsDemushkin.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_of_odd_of_demushkinQ_eq); uniqueness for the other values of q and at p = 2, and that no other pairs occur, remain (Labute 1967).

name: The continuous characters of ℝˣ and ℂˣ
text: every continuous homomorphism ℝˣ → ℂˣ is x ↦ |x|^s sgn(x)^ε for a unique (s, ε) ∈ ℂ × ℤ/2, and every continuous homomorphism [ℂˣ → ℂˣ](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex/ArchimedeanCharacter.html#TauCeti.complexUnitsCharacterEquiv) is z ↦ |z|^s (z/|z|)^k for a unique (s, k) ∈ ℂ × ℤ, as isomorphisms of groups; the input is that a continuous homomorphism ℝ → ℂˣ is t ↦ e^(ts), by lifting through exp with no differentiability assumed; these are the archimedean parameters for the infinity type of the Hecke characters of TauCeti#8468 (Tate's thesis, §2.3).

name: The cup product on singular cohomology
text: Hᵖ(X) × H^q(X) → H^(p+q)(X), with (φ ⌣ ψ)(σ) = φ(σ|[0, …, p])·ψ(σ|[p, …, p+q]), defined through the [Alexander–Whitney map](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/AlexanderWhitney.html#SSet.alexanderWhitney) C(K × L) → C(K) ⊗ C(L) on simplicial sets and singular chains, with the [Leibniz rule](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Monoidal/Cup.html#TauCeti.ChainComplex.d_comp_cupCochain) on cochains, bilinearity and naturality in X; associativity, the unit and graded commutativity are not yet proved (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §3.2).

name: The ring of profinite integers
text: the profinite completion Ẑ of ℤ as a compact, totally disconnected topological commutative ring: a·b is the image of b under the continuous endomorphism taking the generator to a, and ℤ → Ẑ is the integer cast; the projections to ℤ/n and the decomposition over the primes are still to come (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §§2.3, 4.1).

name: The Brauer group as Galois cohomology, and the unramified local invariant
text: Br(F) = H²(G_F, (Fˢ)ˣ) on continuous cohomology, with every class inflated from a finite Galois layer and H²(G_F, μₙ) identified with its n-torsion for n invertible in F; for a finite unramified extension L/K of local fields, inv : H²(Gal(L/K), Lˣ) → ℚ/ℤ is injective with image (1/[L:K])ℤ/ℤ, normalized by arithmetic Frobenius so that the class of a ∈ Kˣ has invariant v(a)/[L:K], compatibly with inflation; the invariant on all of Br(K) is not yet built (Serre, *Local Fields*, XII §1).
the unit ideal gets 0
a prime ideal P gets log N(P)
every positive power P^n also gets log N(P), not log N(P^n), which is what separates it from log N
it vanishes exactly on the ideals that are not prime powers
all primes have density 1
a finite set of primes has density 0
a set has at most one density: it is a limit, not a limit point
the complement of a set of density δ has density 1 − δ
it agrees with Dirichlet density whenever it exists
as a function it is the Hecke slash sum over the double coset
given coset representatives a_i of the double coset, it is the classical sum of the slashes f |[k] a_i
